questions.stem: About Poiseuille's formula Qᵥ = (πR⁴ / 8ηL)·ΔP for a horizontal cylindrical pipe:
options: It is valid only for laminar flows
The volumetric flow rate Qᵥ is proportional to the viscosity η
The pressure P decreases with the distance traveled by the fluid
The pressure P increases along the direction of the flow
ΔP = P₁ − P₂ is called the pressure loss (overpressure)
questions.explanation: Poiseuille's law holds only for laminar flow; ΔP = P₁ − P₂ > 0 is the pressure loss, since P decreases along the path. Qᵥ is inversely proportional to η (η is in the denominator), not proportional.

questions.stem: Laminar flow in a horizontal pipe: the radius R is halved while ΔP, the length L and the viscosity η are unchanged. The volumetric flow rate Qᵥ is:
options: Divided by 2
Divided by 4
Divided by 8
Multiplied by 16
Divided by 16
questions.explanation: Qᵥ = πR⁴ΔP / (8ηL) varies as R⁴, so halving R gives (1/2)⁴ = 1/16 of the flow. Dividing by 4 would be an R² law; a smaller radius can only lower the flow.
questions.mental: Only the R⁴ factor changes: (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. A narrower pipe can't increase the flow, so 'multiplied by 16' is out straight away.

questions.stem: About the hydraulic flow resistance R of a horizontal pipe of length L and radius R₀ (laminar flow):
options: R is proportional to the fourth power of the radius
R = ΔP / Qᵥ
R decreases when the viscosity of the fluid increases
R = 8ηL / (πR₀⁴)
R doubles when the length of the pipe doubles
questions.explanation: R = ΔP/Qᵥ = 8ηL/(πR₀⁴): it is proportional to η and L and inversely proportional to R₀⁴. So a longer pipe or a more viscous fluid raises the resistance, and a wider pipe lowers it.

questions.stem: In the analogy between electricity and the biophysics of fluids:
options: The electric current I corresponds to the pressure P
The electric current I corresponds to the volumetric flow rate Qᵥ
The electrical resistance corresponds to the viscosity η of the fluid
ΔV = V₁ − V₂ > 0 corresponds to ΔP = P₁ − P₂ > 0
Ohm's law ΔV = RI corresponds to ΔP = R·Qᵥ
questions.explanation: Current I ↔ volumetric flow rate Qᵥ, potential difference ΔV ↔ pressure difference ΔP, electrical resistance ↔ hydraulic resistance R, so ΔV = RI ↔ ΔP = RQᵥ. Viscosity is only one factor inside the hydraulic resistance.

questions.stem: A fluid flows in laminar regime through a horizontal pipe with a pressure loss ΔP = 600 Pa and a volumetric flow rate Qᵥ = 2×10⁻⁶ m³/s. Its hydraulic resistance is:
options: 3.3×10⁻⁹ Pa·s/m³
1.2×10⁻³ Pa·s/m³
3×10⁵ Pa·s/m³
3×10⁸ Pa·s/m³
3×10¹¹ Pa·s/m³
questions.explanation: R = ΔP/Qᵥ = 600 / (2×10⁻⁶) = 3×10⁸ Pa·s/m³. 3.3×10⁻⁹ is the inverse ratio Qᵥ/ΔP and 1.2×10⁻³ is the product ΔP·Qᵥ.
questions.mental: 600/2 = 300 = 3×10², and dividing by 10⁻⁶ adds 6 to the exponent: 3×10⁸. A resistance must come out large here (big ΔP over a tiny flow), which already rules out the 10⁻⁹ and 10⁻³ options.

questions.stem: Two compartments (1) and (2), with osmolarities ω₁ and ω₂ and pressures P₁ and P₂, are separated by a membrane. The correct propositions are:
options: If P₁ ≠ P₂, a convective flux Jc of solvent goes from the high-pressure side to the low-pressure side
If ω₁ ≠ ω₂, a diffusive flux Jd of solvent goes from the high-concentration side to the low-concentration side
If P₁ ≠ P₂, a convective flux Jc of solvent goes from the low-pressure side to the high-pressure side
A convective flux of solvent exists only if ω₁ ≠ ω₂
If ω₁ ≠ ω₂, a diffusive flux Jd of solvent goes from the low-concentration side to the high-concentration side
questions.explanation: A concentration difference drives a diffusive solvent flux from low to high concentration; a pressure difference drives a convective solvent flux from high to low pressure. The convective flux depends on P₁ ≠ P₂, not on the osmolarities.

questions.stem: A membrane of thickness l and surface area S has Nₚ pores, cylinders of radius a and length l. The correct propositions are:
options: The number of pores per unit surface area is p = Nₚ / S
The volumetric flow rate through one pore is qᵥ = πa⁴ΔP / (8ηl)
The total volumetric flow rate is Qᵥ = qᵥ / Nₚ
The convective permeability of the membrane is L = p·πa⁴ / (8ηl)
The total volumetric flow rate can be written Qᵥ = S·L·ΔP
questions.explanation: Each pore obeys Poiseuille, qᵥ = πa⁴ΔP/(8ηl); the Nₚ pores add up, Qᵥ = Nₚqᵥ = pSqᵥ = S·(pπa⁴/8ηl)·ΔP = SLΔP. The flows are multiplied by Nₚ, not divided.

questions.stem: About the units used for convective transport:
options: The convective flux Jc is expressed in m³/s
The convective permeability L is expressed in m/(Pa·s)
The convective permeability L is expressed in m/s
The convective flux Jc is expressed in m/s
The hydraulic flow resistance R is expressed in Pa·s/m³
questions.explanation: Jc = Qᵥ/S = LΔP is in m/s, so L = Jc/ΔP is in m/(Pa·s); R = ΔP/Qᵥ is in Pa·s/m³. m³/s is the unit of the volumetric flow rate Qᵥ, and m/s is the unit of Jc, not of L.

questions.stem: About a cylindrical membrane pore of radius a and length l, crossed by a fluid of viscosity η:
options: 8ηl / (πa⁴) is the hydraulic conductance of the pore
πa⁴ / (8ηl) is the hydraulic conductance of the pore
L = p·πa⁴ / (8ηl) is the hydraulic conductance per unit surface area of the membrane
8ηl / (πa⁴) is the hydraulic resistance of the pore
L is the hydraulic resistance per unit surface area of the membrane
questions.explanation: 8ηl/(πa⁴) is the hydraulic resistance of a pore; its inverse πa⁴/(8ηl) is the pore's hydraulic conductance, and multiplying by p gives L, the conductance per unit surface area. L is a conductance, not a resistance.

questions.stem: A membrane of convective permeability L = 2×10⁻¹¹ m/(Pa·s) and surface area S = 2 cm² is subjected to a pressure difference ΔP = 5×10³ Pa. The correct propositions are:
options: The convective flux is Jc = 2.5×10⁸ m/s
The volumetric flow rate is Qᵥ = 2×10⁻¹¹ m³/s
The convective flux is Jc = 1×10⁻⁷ m/s
The volumetric flow rate is Qᵥ = 2×10⁻⁷ m³/s
The convective flux is Jc = 4×10⁻¹⁵ m/s
questions.explanation: Jc = LΔP = 2×10⁻¹¹ × 5×10³ = 10⁻⁷ m/s, and Qᵥ = S·Jc = 2×10⁻⁴ m² × 10⁻⁷ = 2×10⁻¹¹ m³/s. 2×10⁻⁷ forgets to convert cm² to m²; 2.5×10⁸ divides ΔP by L.
questions.mental: 2×5 = 10, exponents −11 + 3 = −8, so Jc = 10×10⁻⁸ = 10⁻⁷ m/s. Then 2 cm² = 2×10⁻⁴ m², times 10⁻⁷ gives 2×10⁻¹¹ m³/s. A flux of 2.5×10⁸ m/s is physically absurd, so that option is out at once.

options: Filtering a solution through a porous membrane makes the solvent move under a pressure gradient while the solute particles are retained
Filtration is driven by the concentration gradient of the solute
Filtration relies on the principle of sieving
Ultrafiltration uses a semi-permeable membrane with a pore diameter between 0.001 µm and 0.1 µm
Ultrafiltration uses a membrane with a pore diameter between 1 µm and 10 µm
questions.explanation: Filtration is the convective solvent flux through a porous membrane: it is driven by a pressure gradient and retains the solutes (sieving). It is called ultrafiltration when the membrane is semi-permeable with pores of 0.001–0.1 µm.

questions.stem: In the figure, the membrane is semi-permeable, ω₁ > ω₂, and an overpressure applied on side (1) gives P₁ > P₂ with ΔP > Δπ. The correct propositions are:
options: The diffusive flux of water Jd goes from (2) to (1)
The net solvent flux goes from (2) to (1)
The convective flux of water Jc goes from (1) to (2)
The diffusive flux is given by Jd = L·ΔP
This situation corresponds to ultrafiltration
questions.explanation: P₁ > P₂ pushes water (1) → (2) with Jc = LΔP; ω₁ > ω₂ pulls water (2) → (1) with Jd = LΔπ. Since ΔP > Δπ, Jc > Jd and the net flux follows Jc, from (1) to (2): this is ultrafiltration.

questions.stem: Across a semi-permeable membrane, with ΔP = P₁ − P₂ and Δπ = (ω₁ − ω₂)RT, the correct propositions are:
options: The effective filtration pressure is Peff = ΔP − Δπ
The effective filtration pressure is Peff = ΔP + Δπ
If ΔP > Δπ, then Jc > Jd
The net solvent flux is Jnet = Jc − Jd = L·Peff
The ultrafiltration rate is Q_uf = S·L·Peff
questions.explanation: The two fluxes are opposed, so Jnet = Jc − Jd = L(ΔP − Δπ) = L·Peff, and Q_uf = S·Jnet = S·L·Peff. The osmotic pressure works against the applied pressure, so it is subtracted, not added.

questions.stem: A semi-permeable membrane (L = 10⁻¹² m/(Pa·s), S = 2 m²) separates two solutions with ω₁ − ω₂ = 0.1 osmol/L at 27 °C. An overpressure ΔP = P₁ − P₂ = 3.5×10⁵ Pa is applied on side (1). (R = 8.31 SI) The correct propositions are:
options: Δπ ≈ 2.5×10⁵ Pa
The effective filtration pressure is Peff ≈ 6×10⁵ Pa
The effective filtration pressure is Peff ≈ 1×10⁵ Pa
The net solvent flux is Jnet ≈ 1×10⁻⁷ m/s
The ultrafiltration rate is Q_uf ≈ 2×10⁻⁷ m³/s
questions.explanation: Δπ = ΔωRT = 100 osmol/m³ × 8.31 × 300 ≈ 2.5×10⁵ Pa; Peff = ΔP − Δπ ≈ 1×10⁵ Pa (6×10⁵ adds them). Jnet = L·Peff ≈ 10⁻⁷ m/s and Q_uf = S·Jnet ≈ 2×10⁻⁷ m³/s.
questions.mental: Convert 0.1 osmol/L to 100 osmol/m³; RT ≈ 8.31 × 300 ≈ 2500, so Δπ ≈ 100 × 2500 = 2.5×10⁵ Pa. Then 3.5 − 2.5 = 1 → Peff = 10⁵ Pa, Jnet = 10⁻¹² × 10⁵ = 10⁻⁷ m/s, and ×2 m² gives 2×10⁻⁷ m³/s.

questions.stem: Across a dialysis membrane, the net solvent flux Jnet carries a solute (s) along with it. The correct propositions are:
options: The convective flux of solute is Jcs = Jnet·C̄s
The mean solute concentration is C̄s = C₁s + C₂s
The diffusive flux of solute is Jds = P·|ΔCs|
The diffusive flux of solute is Jds = L·ΔP
The net solute flux is the vector sum of the convective and diffusive solute fluxes
questions.explanation: The solute is dragged by the solvent, Jcs = Jnet·C̄s with C̄s = (C₁s + C₂s)/2 (the mean, not the sum), and it also diffuses, Jds = P|ΔCs|; the net solute flux is Jcs + Jds (vectors). L·ΔP is the convective flux of solvent.

questions.stem: Across a dialysis membrane, the net solvent flux is Jnet = 2×10⁻⁶ m/s. The solute concentrations are C₁s = 40 mmol/L and C₂s = 10 mmol/L. The convective flux of solute Jcs is:
options: 1×10⁻⁴ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
6×10⁻⁵ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
5×10⁻⁵ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
5×10⁻⁸ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
8×10⁻⁸ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
questions.explanation: C̄s = (40 + 10)/2 = 25 mmol/L = 25 mol/m³, so Jcs = Jnet·C̄s = 2×10⁻⁶ × 25 = 5×10⁻⁵ mol·m⁻²·s⁻¹. 1×10⁻⁴ uses the sum, 6×10⁻⁵ the difference, and 5×10⁻⁸ keeps C̄s in mol/L.
questions.mental: mmol/L = mol/m³, so C̄s = 25 mol/m³ with no conversion. 2 × 25 = 50 → 50×10⁻⁶ = 5×10⁻⁵.
